easy.def: To keep watch so nothing bad happens.
examples: Dogs guard the house.
He guards the gate.
A big dog guarded the sheep.

more.def: To watch over a person, place or thing to keep it safe.
examples: A dog guards the farm at night.
Soldiers guard the old fort.
The goalie guards the net.

easy.def: A person who keeps a place safe.
examples: The guard stood at the door.
A guard checked our bags.
The guard waved.

more.def: A person whose job is to protect a person or place.
examples: A guard stood at the museum door.
The royal guard wore red coats.
The guard checked everyone's ticket.

easy.def: To give an answer when you are not sure.
examples: Can you guess what is in the box?
I guess you are six years old.
Guess which hand has the coin.

more.def: To give an answer or opinion without knowing for certain.
examples: I guessed that there were two hundred beans in the jar.
Can you guess the ending of the story?
I did not know the answer, so I had to guess.
We have a guest.
The guest sat down.
Guests came to the party.

more.def: A person who is invited to visit or stay somewhere.
examples: We set an extra place for our guest.
The guests arrived at six.
The hotel guest asked for a towel.
The lights guide the ships.
Mom guides the baby's hand.
A map will guide us.

more.def: To lead or show the way to someone.
examples: A ranger guided us along the trail to the waterfall.
The stars guided sailors across the sea long ago.
A helper guided the new student to her classroom.

easy.def: Feeling bad because you did something wrong.
examples: I feel guilty about the mess.
He felt guilty.
She looked guilty.

more.def: Feeling ashamed because you know you did something wrong.
examples: I felt guilty when I ate the last cookie.
The dog looked guilty beside the torn pillow.
She felt guilty for forgetting her friend's birthday.

easy.def: A tool that shoots small metal balls.
examples: A gun is loud.
The police have a gun.
He saw a gun in the museum.

more.def: A weapon that shoots bullets, which can hurt people and animals.
examples: The museum has an old gun from long ago.
A police officer carries a gun for work.
On the old farm, a gun hung over the fireplace.
The doctor looked at the guts.
The guts digest food.
The fish was cleaned of its guts.

more.def: The tubes in the middle of the body where food is digested.
examples: The fisherman cleaned the fish and took out its guts.
The guts of an animal break down the food it eats.
A snake's guts are long and thin.
It takes guts to jump.
She has guts.
He had the guts to speak up.

more.def: Courage, or the strength to do something that is hard or scary.
examples: It took guts to speak in front of the whole school.
She had the guts to try the high diving board.
He showed guts when he stood up to the bully.
That guy has a big dog.
The guy at the shop was nice.
He is a funny guy.

more.def: A boy or man, in everyday talk, or a friendly way to speak to a group.
examples: The guy who drives the school bus knows all our names.
He is a friendly guy who loves to tell jokes.
Come on, guys, it is time to go!
